method: Country-specific conservative design inference from dated institutional/equipment evidence. Years are ceilings for selected supported domains, not a blanket all-technologies-by-year grant. Local release floors are not claims of historical sovereignty. No later deliveries or experimental programme are automatically operational technology.

AFR.rationale: The Sierra Leone AFRC is a 1997 formation. Its placeholder receives only an old local light-force floor; later civil-war weapons are excluded.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

AGL.rationale: For a potential 1970 release, retain local ports, rail/workshop and light-industry know-how alongside the liberation war's small-arms environment. exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No independent Angolan state in January 1970; no post-1975 Soviet/Cuban inventory.

Coastal patrol capabilities do not imply an ocean-going frigate industry.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No nuclear reactor, submarine, MiG-23/25, attack helicopter or 1970s industrial expansion.
Do not infer ballistic or cruise-missile production from imported Komar/Osa craft.
The documented pre-cutoff SA-2 system grants only the 1955 SAM foundation; no 1965 SAM0/SA-3 step is inferred for 1 January 1970.

No Ogbunigwe-to-ballistic-missile leap; improvised weapons are not a strategic delivery system.

exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No 1977 inventory package, independent fighter manufacture, advanced missiles or nuclear branch.

SSU.name: South Sudan
SSU.rationale: A southern Sudanese release during the first civil-war period; keep local light-force and elementary works capabilities below the central state's imported military systems.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

STH.name: St Helena
STH.rationale: Only a minimal local civil-works and security floor is appropriate. British possession and oceanic location do not demonstrate local capacity to design or support complex military systems.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No autonomous army, combat-aircraft, naval-warship or strategic research.

SUD.name: Sudan
SUD.rationale: Retain an older British-derived army and small aviation/coastal-service foundation. Later Soviet and Chinese procurement cannot be assumed fully operational at 1 January; use a conservative early-jet ceiling while preserving basic imported artillery and vehicle support.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No comprehensive 1970s Soviet/Chinese modernization or later local arms industry.

SWA.name: Swaziland
SWA.rationale: Use an elementary police/security and light-processing baseline at the start of independence. Neither the later defense force nor South African grid connections from 1973 are present capability on 1 January 1970.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No post-1970 army or aircraft package; no modern dispatch from later imported power.

SWS.name: South West State of Somalia
SWS.rationale: A hypothetical Somali inland release uses a sparse local light-force baseline; modern federal-state institutions must not be projected backward.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

TIE.name: Tibesti
TIE.rationale: A remote Chadian regional release; a sparse local workshop/security floor is more defensible than a modern national defense catalogue.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

TNZ.name: Tanzania
TNZ.rationale: The defense force was reorganized after the 1964 union and mutiny. Favor infantry, transport and basic technical support; imported training/air-transport assistance does not establish a 1965 combat-aircraft industry. Development projects planned in 1969 are kept distinct from completed capability.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No TAZARA completion, future Chinese fighter fleet, modern SAMs or heavy industrial research from aid pledges.

TOG.name: Togo
TOG.rationale: A small coastal service and narrow processing sector permit basic maritime, infantry and vehicle knowledge. Keep specialist weapons and industrial electronics unresearched rather than inferring them from aid relationships.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.

TRP.name: Tripolitania
TRP.rationale: Urban/coastal Libyan release with basic port and workshop knowledge, without an autonomous post-1970 aircraft or missile programme.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

TUA.name: Tuaregs
TUA.rationale: A Saharan regional release represents light-force and caravan/road support, without inheriting the full inventories of several parent states.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
Hypothetical release baseline only, not a claim that the modern entity or an autonomous research establishment existed in January 1970.
No inherited full parent-state military, nuclear, aerospace or naval catalogue.

TUN.name: Tunisia
TUN.rationale: A small post-independence force and light manufacturing base warrant selective 1940s-1950s capabilities, not the comprehensive package of its larger neighbors. Imported training and liaison aviation are treated conservatively rather than as evidence of local jet manufacture.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No later F-5 fleet, missile/naval modernization or domestic aircraft industry.

UGA.name: Uganda
UGA.rationale: A small army with inherited British support practices and emerging imported aviation warrants basic post-war infantry and vehicle knowledge. Keep heavy armor, electronics and aircraft manufacture low where the delivery record is uncertain.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No MiG-21 or 1970s military expansion; landlocked service does not grant a marine warship tree.

UNI.name: UNITA
UNI.rationale: A guerrilla organization in the Portuguese colonial war supports imported light arms, basic communications and improvised repair. Later conventional equipment and foreign interventions are not knowledge available to this movement at the start of 1970.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No post-1975 armored force, advanced SAMs, Stinger, jet aircraft or strategic missiles.

VER.name: Cape Verde
VER.rationale: The port/administrative and small security baseline is kept separate from Portugal's military research. A future independent island state should not begin with modern combat aircraft or a navy's full construction catalogue.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No independent state or advanced military industry at cutoff.

ZAM.name: Zambia
ZAM.rationale: Copper mining and the joint CAPCO system support machinery and regional-power knowledge above the rural baseline. Military knowledge stays selective because a mining enclave and expatriate technical support do not supply a complete local defense industry.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No future MiG-21 fleet, Kafue Gorge or Kariba North completion as January 1970 assets.
Hydro knowledge represents shared operating institutions, not domestic turbine manufacture.

ZAN.name: Zanzibar
ZAN.rationale: A hypothetical release inherits island civil works and a narrow revolutionary/light-force equipment base. It does not inherit a full modern Tanzania, Chinese or Soviet research tree merely from political assistance.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No independent sovereign state at cutoff, modern frigate or fighter-production industry.

ZIM.name: Zimbabwe / Rhodesia
ZIM.rationale: Rhodesia had a comparatively developed manufacturing, rail and electric-power economy, but depended on imported aircraft and armor. The shared Kariba/CAPCO system predates 1970. Avoid importing the intensive later Bush War vehicle, helicopter and special-operations adaptations.
exclusions: No automatic grant from modern imported equipment lists; this is a conservative January 1970 knowledge and support baseline.
No later mine-protected-vehicle catalogue, Fireforce system, locally designed modern fighter or Zimbabwe's post-1980 weapons.
